*Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 35* (titled *Thūpakata*, translated by Bhikkhu Sujato as "35. Making food into a heap") is a training rule (*sekhiya*) governing monastic dining etiquette found in the Vinaya Piṭaka of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. It regulates proper conduct regarding not heaping up food into a mound when receiving or eating alms, and has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

The rule belongs to a widely preserved core of monastic discipline. SuttaCentral identifies extensive parallels across virtually all surviving Vinaya lineages, including the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Sekhiya 35), *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and the *Parivāra*, as well as the corresponding *prātimokṣa* and *vibhaṅga* texts of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral].
